-Recent meetings with state officials and organization leaders

events.description:
Raising kids in a fast-changing, tech-driven world can feel overwhelming. Dr. Jared Cooney Horvath, a neuroscientist and Harvard educator who has worked with more than 1,000 schools, offers clear, practical answers for families of kids in K–12. Each evening is a 90-minute presentation followed by a 30-minute live Q&A, so bring your questions.

You'll leave knowing:
-What builds kids' attention, memory, and real understanding, and what gets in the way
-How to tell healthy challenge from harmful stress
-Concrete things you can do at home, and ask about at school, including around technology

Dr. Horvath (PhD, MEd) is a Harvard-trained neuroscientist and educator and the founder of LME Global. He has worked with schools, universities, and governments in more than 30 countries and is the author of six books, including The Digital Delusion, and more than 60 research articles. His work has been featured by CNN, the BBC, The Atlantic, The Free Press, and C-SPAN.

Hosted by the Wellesley Mothers Forum and cosponsored by the Wellesley Education Foundation, Beyond Screens Wellesley,  LexKidsBeKids, The Lexington Education Foundation, and Turning Life On.

This event is financially sponsored by Turning Life On, a MA Coalition of parent-led groups working together to change the norms around how we live with technology. Turning Life On is a registered 501(c)3. Every donation you make helps fund events like this.

This event is also happening in Concord on Nov. 17, visit the events page to register for that event.

events.description:
Join us for a free screening of the film "Your Attention Please: Reclaiming Humanity in the Digital Age", followed by a community discussion led by a panel of local experts. 

A new generation of parents, teens, and reformers are fighting back against Big Tech’s agenda to define the future of human connection. From Kristin, a mother pursuing legislative reform after losing her son, to Trisha, a young programmer building technology to stop cyberbullying, the film reveals how deeply the attention economy is shaping childhood, mental health, and human connection.

As lawmakers debate social media reform, Gen Z launches a global Offline Club movement, and a high school dares to go phone-free. What emerges is not a doomsday story, but a hopeful one: proof that the attention crisis is not inevitable and that a cultural shift is already underway.

Blending intimate human stories with insights from leading experts in tech reform and digital wellbeing, Your Attention Please asks some of the most urgent questions of our time: Can we reclaim our autonomy? Can technology be redesigned to serve humanity? And what does a healthier relationship with the digital world look like for us and our kids?
